findings.title: `float: right` on .small-action button is inert now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` now gets `@include flexbox()` (display:flex), which makes float declarations on its direct children no-ops. The `button` child still relies on `float: right` to be pushed to the right edge of the small-action row (e.g. the undo/delete control). With flex layout the button becomes a normal flex item sized to its content and will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which is now dead code.

findings.title: Removing vertical padding from .small-action-desc can let the floated avatar overflow
findings.body: `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, but `.small-action-desc .avatar` (line 298) is still floated. A float does not contribute to the height of its block container, so with zero vertical padding the flex item's height is only the text line height; if the avatar is taller than one line of the 0.9em text it will overflow the flex item and overlap neighbouring content. Previously the 0.5em padding plus 5px margin absorbed the difference. Consider clearing the float or using flex/inline-block for the avatar instead.

findings.title: .panel loses right alignment on the legacy box model the flexbox mixin targets
findings.body: `.panel` replaced `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)`. `margin-left: auto` only pushes a flex item to the end in the modern flexbox spec; the `flexbox()` mixin deliberately also emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box` for old WebKit/Gecko, where auto margins are not honoured in the box model. In those browsers the header panel (notification/search/user icons) will now render left-aligned right after the title instead of at the right edge. Either drop the legacy `display` fallbacks or add `-webkit-box-pack: end` / `-ms-flex-pack: end` on `.contents`.

findings.title: align-items mixin passes modern values straight to legacy properties and omits -moz-box-align
findings.body: `align-items($alignment)` forwards the value verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties only accept `start | center | end | baseline | stretch`. Any future call with the spec values `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, etc. will emit invalid declarations that old browsers drop silently, so the legacy prefixes give a false sense of coverage (and the invalid value is easy to miss because the standard `align-items` still works). The mixin also never emits `-moz-box-align`, even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so legacy Gecko gets box layout with no alignment. Finally, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any browser and is dead output. Consider mapping values (e.g. `flex-start` -> `start`) or dropping the legacy prefixes entirely.

findings.title: order mixin maps directly onto 1-based box-ordinal-group
findings.body: `order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` with the same number as `order`. The legacy ordinal-group property is 1-based (minimum value 1, default 1) while `order` is 0-based with default 0, so any call with `order(0)` or a negative value (both legal for `order`) produces an invalid legacy declaration, and relative ordering between items that set `order` and items that do not can differ between the legacy and modern code paths. If the legacy prefixes are kept, the value should be offset/validated; otherwise they should be dropped.

findings.title: inline-flex mixin forces legacy box layout where a safe inline-block fallback existed
findings.body: `.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously declared only `display: inline-flex`, so browsers without flexbox support simply kept `display: inline-block` from the `.badge-wrapper` rule and rendered correctly. The new `inline-flex()` mixin additionally emits `display: -webkit-inline-box` / `-moz-inline-box` / `-ms-inline-flexbox`, which those same old browsers *do* understand, switching the bullet badges to the legacy box model with different sizing/shrinking rules (relevant here because `span.badge-category` relies on `max-width`, `overflow: hidden` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`). This is a rendering change for old browsers that was previously handled gracefully; verify it or drop the legacy display fallbacks.
